hypothesis: Large language models (LLMs) could enhance drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction by leveraging their ability to process and generate complex language-based data, potentially improving the accuracy of binding affinity predictions. This hypothesis is supported by the robustness and inference capabilities of LLMs, which have been shown to drive and suppress human language networks effectively [centaur:42], and the success of deep learning models, such as those using CNNs, in predicting DTI binding affinities from sequence information [deepdta:0]. Integrating LLMs with existing deep learning architectures could thus offer a novel approach to refining DTI predictions.
